name: management-bar
title: Management Bar
description: A small rounded toolbar for reviewing candidates: chevrons around a page count, three colour-coded icon actions, and a teal button that names the stage it moves the item to, with a keyboard shortcut keycap.
use: Reviewers need quick approve, reject and move actions beside a paged list.
avoid: Action words appear only on hover, so touch users see bare icons and must guess what they do.
a11y: Icon buttons have aria-labels and the chevrons disable at the ends, but words show on hover only, there is no focus style, and no reduced-motion check. (keyboard: partial, labels: good, reduced motion: not handled)
looks: One rounded dark bar on a black page. It opens with a left chevron, a two-digit page counter and a right chevron, then a grey ban icon, a red cross and a green card icon, and ends with a wide teal button reading Move to: Interview, I with a small command-E keycap.
behaves: The chevrons step the page number, which rolls like a dial and disables at either end. Hovering an icon button widens it so its word slides in beside the icon, and the teal move button dips slightly when pressed.
customise: Nothing is exposed: the page total, the action labels, the destination stage and the shortcut are written in, so adapting it means editing the component.
weight: light: A short row of buttons with spring width and digit-roll transitions that idle at rest.
demo: Heading "Senior Product Designer" with "Candidate review · Priya Raman · Applied 3 days ago" and page 3 of 10.
issues: At rest the three actions are bare icons, so the bar's options are unclear until hovered.
The page counter changes without any live-region announcement for screen readers.
polishWhy: Tight toolbar with an expanding-label flourish; hover-only wording and no focus cues cost it.
